name: empty-dns-excluded-rejects-everything-invalid
description: An empty-IA5String dNSName excluded subtree is treated as 'matches any DNS name' by NSS-lineage validators, rejecting every leaf with a DNS SAN. RFC 5280 4.2.1.10 does not normatively specify what an empty constraint base means; the convention is the mirror image of empty-permitted-allows-everything.
references: Go name_constraints_test "empty DNS excluded constraint rejects everything"
notes: OpenSSL: nc_dns returns OK for an empty base, so an empty excluded base matches every DNS SAN and the chain is rejected.
Go: dnsConstraints.all short-circuits the query to a match, and because this is the excluded set the verdict flips to 'excluded'.
GnuTLS: check_dns_constraints special-cases the empty excluded entry with the comment 'the CA shouldn't have issued a certificate with a DNSNAME' and returns false.
